questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. These items protect you from injury.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement offers the best traction.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your side vision.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Keep a steady speed and ride straight. Zigzagging to stop the weave is dangerous because it takes you out of your lane.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. That is why proper use of signals is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, maintain a minimum ______ following distance.
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-second
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least a two-second distance behind the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to provide a better grip on the handgrips.
Not be worn because they make it harder to work the controls.
Be worn only on cooler days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to provide a better grip on the handgrips.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves made of leather or another durable material. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: To lower the risk of a crash:

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in parts of the lane where you are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and constantly scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to be a problem.
Have blind spots that require head checks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do about lane position?

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Move around the lane constantly to keep other drivers away.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Adjust your position based on how road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: How important is clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
It should not fully cover your arms or legs.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but loose enough so you can move easily.

questions.question: What is an advantage of downshifting smoothly on a motorcycle?

options.text: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
You should not do it if other vehicles are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Smooth downshifting uses engine power to help slow the motorcycle. If you do this, use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: Is riding at night easier or harder than riding during the day?

options.text: Easier because you can see other vehicles' lights better.
Harder because it is difficult to see.
It is not allowed on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because it is difficult to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well as during the day. Without normal shadows and light, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during daylight. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Ride on the shoulder to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Always wear bright clothing so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: How can carrying a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It makes no difference to how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It is encouraged for all riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Your friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use empty roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Take their keys if needed and help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: What type of sign is usually rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What is the correct body position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly at the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean forward so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly at the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips. This lets you easily reach and control the motorcycle.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. It is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This means your bike will speed up slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, begin stopping sooner, increase your space from other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps in traffic before crossing or merging.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve visibility?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Other drivers will see you better if you wear bright colors with reflective material. Also keep your headlight on at all times and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is an advantage of a leather jacket?

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, for protection while riding. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you cool even in hot weather.
